notes: Nine non-CONFIRMED/non-UNVERIFIABLE claims re-checked against the live DB (provenance.forecast_metrics, forecast_eval, quantile_coverage, eda_metric, eda_burst_episode) plus the archived run logs under /home/gio/tese/predictors/results/logs/. Four first-pass verdicts overturned to CONFIRMED (175, 191, 335, 382) because the thesis statements are literally true under an ordinary hedging/rounding convention. Five defects survive: the per-forecast GPU-ms double count (96), the onset-component WAPE ranges (252), the TimesFM quantile attribution (282), the non-image p10 coverage upper bound (303), and the 'one-third at sub-minute bins' summary overreach (411). Two of the surviving five had first-pass fixes that were themselves wrong or imprecise and are corrected here.

rulings.quote: averaged over a configuration's ${\approx}54$k origins, one 12-step forecast costs ${\approx}65$ (Chronos-2) to ${\approx}90$ (Toto-2) milliseconds of GPU time, comfortably inside any 15--60-second decision cadence.
rulings.evidence: Re-derived from the archived per-part log lines (predictors/results/logs/*.log, regex '\[(model) (mode) (res)\] part i/n: N origins, R rows in Ts'), summed per (model,mode): chronos/uni 54,035 origins / 697.8 s = 12.91 ms per origin; chronos/cov 54,035 / 2752.4 s = 50.94 ms; toto/uni 55,740 / 2383.6 s = 42.76 ms; toto/cov 55,740 / 2364.8 s = 42.43 ms; timesfm/uni 56,595 / 236.8 s = 4.18 ms. Every part emits 48 rows per origin (4 variates x 12 horizon steps), so one origin = one 12-step forecast of all four signals. The published 65/90 are exactly reproduced by dividing the TWO-configuration model totals (chronos 3450.2 s, toto 4748.4 s) by a ONE-configuration origin count: 3450.2/54035 = 63.9 ms, 4748.4/55740 = 85.2 ms. That those totals are two-configuration sums is confirmed by the immediately preceding sentence in the same paragraph, which correctly reports them as the per-model wall-clock ('roughly one hour and 80 minutes': 3450.2 s = 57.5 min, 4748.4 s = 79.1 min). The defect is therefore proven internally, not just externally: the same two numbers are used correctly one sentence earlier and double-counted one sentence later. DB cross-check: SELECT model,mode,count(*) FROM provenance.forecast_metrics WHERE span='common' AND candidate='point' AND h=-1 GROUP BY 1,2 -> eight model/mode configurations, matching the eight log streams.
rulings.final_fix: Replace with: "averaged over a configuration's \num{54000}--\num{56600} origins, one 12-step forecast of all four signals costs \SI{4}{\milli\second} (TimesFM) to \SI{51}{\milli\second} (Chronos-2 with covariates) of GPU time, comfortably inside any 15--60-second decision cadence." Justification: per-configuration ms/origin from the archived logs = 4.18 (timesfm/uni), 12.91 (chronos/uni), 42.43 (toto/cov), 42.76 (toto/uni), 50.94 (chronos/cov). The conclusion is unaffected and strengthened.

rulings.quote: The spreads are small (typically under 2 WAPE points), and several bolded column wins are decided by $\leq$0.1 WAPE point over 167 origins
rulings.evidence: Query: WITH r AS (SELECT resolution,variate,model,mode,wape FROM provenance.forecast_metrics WHERE span='common' AND candidate='point' AND h=-1 AND model IN ('timesfm','chronos','toto')) SELECT resolution,variate,(max(wape)-min(wape))*100 FROM r GROUP BY 1,2. Result: 16 of the 20 resolution x signal cells have a foundation-model spread under 2 WAPE points (1min 0.213-0.640; 30s 0.797-1.991; 45s 0.528-2.010 with only 45s images at 2.010; 15s 0.914-4.326; 1s 3.372-21.711). The referent of 'the spreads' is the 20-cell grid the two preceding sentences enumerate ('takes 15 of the 20 cells', 'all twelve at 30 s and finer'), and 16/20 = 80 percent satisfies the hedge 'typically'. The chapter separately and explicitly acknowledges the sub-minute exception at line 386 ('the inter-model gaps are larger in the sub-minute shot-noise regime'), so there is no internal contradiction. Second half verified exactly: best-vs-second gaps for the eight bolded table columns are 1min ctx 0.036, requests 0.041, images 0.058, gen 0.257; 1s images 0.000, requests 0.073, ctx 0.190, gen 0.510 -- five of the eight bolded wins are decided by <=0.1 point, which is 'several'. Origin count verified: SELECT n_origins_used FROM provenance.forecast_eval WHERE resolution='1min' -> 167.
rulings.final_fix: NO EDIT. 'Typically under 2 WAPE points' is a hedged statement that holds in 16 of the 20 grid cells, and the '<=0.1 point over 167 origins' half is exact. OPTIONAL sharpening only (not a correction, both halves DB-verified): "The spreads are small at provisioning cadence (under 0.7 WAPE points in every \SI{1}{\minute} column, though up to 21.7 points at \SI{1}{\second} bins), and several bolded column wins are decided by $\leq$0.1 WAPE point over 167 origins".

rulings.quote: At \SI{1}{\minute} the best shipped predictor (ARIMA, 0.521 WAPE at the first horizon step) ties the classical baselines and trails the best foundation model (0.515, same step) by about a WAPE point
rulings.evidence: Query: SELECT family,predictor,round(wape::numeric,5),n_origins_used FROM provenance.forecast_eval WHERE resolution='1min' ORDER BY wape. Result: toto/uni 0.51530, chronos/cov 0.52100, arima 0.52132 (167 origins), ewma 0.52170, prophet 0.52638, kalman 0.53992, holt_winters 0.59460, naive 0.61800, constant 0.61800. Every quoted number is exact: ARIMA 0.52132 -> 0.521, best FM 0.51530 -> 0.515, 'ties the classical baselines' (EWMA 0.52170, a 0.0004 difference), and the constant predictor reproducing naive exactly (0.61800 vs 0.61800). The gap is 0.00602 = 0.602 WAPE points. 'About a WAPE point' is stated at one-significant-figure integer precision, and 0.6 rounds to 1 under the ordinary convention this audit has already accepted elsewhere; both operands are printed in the same sentence so the exact gap is recoverable by the reader. The 15 s continuation is also exact: ARIMA 0.66751 -> 0.668, best FM toto/cov 0.63740 -> 0.637, kalman 0.81110 -> 0.811, naive 0.76380 -> 0.764, prophet 0.73283 -> 0.733; the described 'widening' (0.6 -> 3.1 points) is correct in the same unit.
rulings.final_fix: NO EDIT. All four quoted WAPE values are exact to the published precision and the gap description is defensible at the stated integer precision (0.602 -> 'about a' point). OPTIONAL precision improvement only: "...trails the best foundation model (0.515, same step) by 0.6 WAPE points".

rulings.quote: \emph{at} the onsets the image forecast is the \emph{worst} component (75--100\% WAPE, against 58--72\% for the direct context forecast and 33--38\% for requests)
rulings.evidence: Source of record: /home/gio/tese/predictors/results/metrics/additive_structural_ablation.json, key component_forecastability_at_onsets (subset onset_steep_image_rise), four entries: chronos/1min (images 0.75116, requests 0.37681, ctx_direct 0.57790), toto/1min (0.73326, 0.32829, 0.56542), chronos/15s (0.99647, 0.37485, 0.71636), toto/15s (1.00132, 0.37477, 0.71569). Full ranges: images 73.33-100.13, ctx_direct 56.54-71.64, requests 32.83-37.68. The published requests range (33-38) demonstrably includes Toto-2 (32.83 -> 33), so the sentence is NOT scoped to Chronos-2; yet the images and ctx lower bounds (75, 58) are the Chronos-2-only minima and exclude Toto-2's 73.33 and 56.54. Mixed-scope interval, not a rounding artifact: 73.33 cannot round or bracket to 75, and 56.54 cannot round or bracket to 58. Not a DB staleness case -- no superseding artifact exists; no other run of additive_structural_ablation.py is archived outside the two agent worktree copies, which are byte-identical in these fields.
rulings.final_fix: Replace with: "the image forecast is the \emph{worst} component (73--100\% WAPE, against 57--72\% for the direct context forecast and 33--38\% for requests)". All six bounds are the rounded archived extrema: images 73.33/100.13, ctx_direct 56.54/71.64, requests 32.83/37.68.

rulings.quote: TimesFM's mean head is beaten in 18 of its 20 cells (median improvement $-1.7\%$, always by a below-median quantile, modally p40), and the Gaussian-band baselines account for 31 more (up to $-45\%$ for Holt--Winters on 1-second images, where a p10 path simply undoes the model's burst overshoot).
rulings.evidence: Query: WITH p AS (SELECT model,mode,resolution,variate,wape pw FROM provenance.forecast_metrics WHERE span='common' AND h=-1 AND candidate='point'), q AS (SELECT model,mode,resolution,variate,min(wape) qw,(array_agg(candidate ORDER BY wape))[1] bestq FROM provenance.forecast_metrics WHERE span='common' AND h=-1 AND candidate<>'point' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4) SELECT model,count(*) FILTER (WHERE qw<pw), percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (qw-pw)/pw) FILTER (WHERE qw<pw), min((qw-pw)/pw) FROM p JOIN q USING(model,mode,resolution,variate) GROUP BY 1. Results: timesfm 18/20 beaten, median -1.679%, best -17.04%; ewma 9, holt_winters 16, naive 6 (sum 31); chronos 2/40 (median -0.044%), toto 0/40. Total 51. Every count and the -1.7% median are exact. Holt-Winters 1 s images: p10 118.91 vs point 217.04 = -45.21%, and p10 is indeed the winning candidate -- exact. What fails is the quantile attribution: grouping the same join by (model,bestq) gives timesfm p50 = 17 cells, p10 = 1 cell (1 s images, -17.04%); p40 NEVER wins a TimesFM cell. p40 is the modal winner across all 51 cells (ewma 6 + holt_winters 8 + chronos 2 + naive 2 = 18), which is the conflation. 'Always by a BELOW-median quantile' is also wrong: 17 of the 18 wins are AT the median (p50). Note the first pass named p30 as the one non-p50 TimesFM winner; the DB says p10 -- that error is corrected here.
rulings.final_fix: Replace with: "TimesFM's mean head is beaten in 18 of its 20 cells (median improvement $-1.7\%$, always by the median or a lower quantile --- the p50 head in 17 of the 18, p10 in the last, 1-second images), and the Gaussian-band baselines account for 31 more (up to $-45\%$ for Holt--Winters on 1-second images, where a p10 path simply undoes the model's burst overshoot)." Do NOT write 'p30': the DB gives p10 for the 1-second images cell (99.94 vs 120.47 point WAPE, -17.04%). The correction strengthens the following sentence's explanation, since p50 winning is exactly what 'the conditional median already sits below the mean' predicts.

rulings.quote: Median coverage sits at 0.43--0.48, and the lower edge is distorted by zero-inflation ... reading as 0.14--0.21 coverage on images against 0.07--0.13 on the other signals.
rulings.evidence: Query: SELECT model,signal,(detail->'1min'->>'cov10')::float,(detail->'1min'->>'cov50')::float,(detail->'1min'->>'cov90')::float FROM provenance.quantile_coverage ORDER BY signal,model (20 rows = 5 configs x 4 signals). p50: 0.435-0.484 -> '0.43--0.48' CONFIRMED. p90: 0.880-0.898 -> '0.88--0.90' CONFIRMED, and the parenthetical 'Chronos-2 with covariates on images: 0.888' is exact -- which proves the sentence's scope INCLUDES the covariate configurations. Images p10: 0.142 (toto) to 0.213 (chronos) -> '0.14--0.21' CONFIRMED. Non-image p10: min 0.072 (timesfm/gen), max 0.144 (chronos_cov/ctx); also chronos_cov/requests 0.132 and chronos_cov/gen 0.127. The published upper bound 0.13 excludes 0.144, which rounds to 0.14 and cannot bracket to 0.13 under any convention. Since the same sentence's p90 parenthetical names a covariate configuration, the 0.144 row cannot be excluded on scope grounds. Small but real.
rulings.final_fix: Replace the final clause with: "reading as 0.14--0.21 coverage on images against 0.07--0.14 on the other signals." Justification: non-image 1-minute p10 coverage spans 0.072 (TimesFM, generated tokens) to 0.144 (Chronos-2 with covariates, context tokens). Change ONLY the 0.13; the 0.43--0.48 and 0.14--0.21 ranges are exact and must not be touched.

rulings.quote: a scaler holding capacity 12 minutes too long is a far cheaper failure than one arriving 6 minutes late to a median-onset burst
rulings.evidence: Query: SELECT count(*), percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY value_num), min(value_num), max(value_num) FROM provenance.eda_metric WHERE metric_path ~ '^episodes\[[0-9]+\]\.onset_min$' -> n=18, median 6.5, min 1, max 404. This is the 18-episode set that Figure fig:eda-onsets is built on ('Burst onset speed across the 18 episodes', trace-eda.tex:302), and trace-eda.tex:290 reads 'baseline-to-peak in a median of \SI{6}{\minute} (10th percentile \SI{2}{\minute}, fastest \SI{1}{\minute})' -- the p10=2 and min=1 both match the same 18 rows exactly, confirming the row selection. Flooring the exact median 6.5 to 6 is an ordinary convention and is the CONSERVATIVE direction for a quantity the chapter uses as a scaling-decision budget. The alternative table, eda_burst_episode, contains 24 rows all of episode_kind='merged' (median 9.00) -- a different, wider episode set, not the one the figure or either chapter reports.
rulings.final_fix: NO EDIT, in predictors.tex or trace-eda.tex. The 6-minute figure is the floor of the exact 6.5-minute median over the 18-episode set the EDA figure uses, and the predictors sentence is a qualitative cost comparison that inherits it consistently. Under no circumstances substitute the 9-minute median from provenance.eda_burst_episode: that is 24 merged episodes, a different population.

rulings.quote: TimesFM-2.0, however, \emph{predates} the release entirely and lands within ${\approx}2$ WAPE points of the other two at provisioning cadence (1-minute bins), bounding any contamination advantage at about that size
rulings.evidence: Query: WITH t AS (SELECT variate,wape w FROM provenance.forecast_metrics WHERE span='common' AND candidate='point' AND h=-1 AND resolution='1min' AND model='timesfm'), o AS (SELECT variate,min(wape) w FROM provenance.forecast_metrics WHERE span='common' AND candidate='point' AND h=-1 AND resolution='1min' AND model IN ('chronos','toto') GROUP BY 1) SELECT t.variate,(t.w-o.w)*100 FROM t JOIN o USING(variate). Result (best over BOTH uni and cov modes of the other two, the strictest comparison): ctx -0.036, requests +0.041, gen +0.386, images +0.472. Maximum gap 0.472 WAPE points, and TimesFM is the outright winner on 1-minute context tokens. The claim as written is an UPPER BOUND ('within ~2 points'), and 0.472 < 2 -- the statement is true. A conservative bound that is satisfied with 4x margin is not a wrong number; it is a weaker claim than the data supports. The chapter's parenthetical about larger sub-minute gaps is also correct (1 s FM spreads reach 21.7 points).
rulings.final_fix: NO EDIT required -- the claim is true as stated (measured maximum 1-minute inter-model gap 0.472 WAPE points, well inside the ~2-point bound). OPTIONAL strengthening, fully DB-backed: "lands within 0.5 WAPE points of the other two at provisioning cadence (1-minute bins) --- and is itself the best model on the context-token signal --- bounding any contamination advantage at half a WAPE point where the forecasts are consumed".

rulings.quote: beat the fixed-parameter classical baselines on all four demand signals in every cell of the $5{\times}4$ resolution--signal grid: a modest 2--9\% relative edge at provisioning cadence, one-third relative at sub-minute bins
rulings.evidence: Query: WITH f AS (SELECT resolution,variate,min(wape) fw FROM provenance.forecast_metrics WHERE span='common' AND candidate='point' AND h=-1 AND model IN ('timesfm','chronos','toto') GROUP BY 1,2), b AS (SELECT resolution,variate,min(wape) bw FROM provenance.forecast_metrics WHERE span='common' AND candidate='point' AND h=-1 AND model IN ('ewma','naive','holt_winters') GROUP BY 1,2) SELECT resolution,variate,((bw-fw)/bw)*100 FROM f JOIN b USING(resolution,variate). All 20 cells positive -> '20 of 20' CONFIRMED. Computed from UNROUNDED wape, not from the table cells. 1 min: images 2.30, ctx 3.30, requests 5.03, gen 9.27 -> '2--9%' CONFIRMED. Sub-minute: 45 s 7.91-10.64; 30 s 8.87-11.31; 15 s 13.32-16.39; 1 s requests 7.58, gen 18.33, ctx 18.84, images 32.40. 'One-third relative at sub-minute bins' is reached in exactly 1 of the 16 sub-minute cells (1 s images, 32.40%); the four-signal mean at 1 s is 19.3% and at 45 s only 9.2%. The body text at line 154 states this correctly and scoped ('at \SI{1}{\second} the best model forecasts images at 98.8\% WAPE against 146.1\% for EWMA ... a one-third relative reduction'); the summary drops the scope. Defect proven by the chapter's own correctly-scoped body sentence.
rulings.final_fix: Replace with: "a modest 2--9\% relative edge at provisioning cadence, widening to 8--32\% at 1-second bins --- one-third on the image signal, where WAPE${\approx}100\%$ marks the no-skill floor". Justification: 1-minute relative edge 2.30-9.27%; 1-second relative edge 7.58% (requests) to 32.40% (images). Do not extend 'one-third' to the 15/30/45-second bins, where the edge is 7.9-16.4%.

rejected_fixes: 1) Line 282, first pass proposed '... the p50 head in 17 of the 18, p30 in the last'. REJECTED as to 'p30': the DB gives p10 as the winning candidate for TimesFM on 1-second images (p10 WAPE 99.94 vs point 120.47, -17.04%); p30 does not win any TimesFM cell. Applying the first-pass text would replace one wrong quantile label with another. 2) Line 335, first pass proposed amending trace-eda.tex:290 to 'a median of 6.5 minutes'. REJECTED as unnecessary: 6 is the floor of the exact 6.5-minute median over the 18-episode set, an accepted bracketing convention, and the change would ripple into predictors.tex:335 and the planner chapter for no accuracy gain. The related suggestion to use the eda_burst_episode median of 9 minutes must be rejected outright -- that table holds 24 episode_kind='merged' rows, a different population from the 18 episodes the EDA figure and both chapters report. 3) Line 191, first pass proposed rewriting to 'by 0.6 WAPE points (1.2% relative)'. REJECTED as a mandatory fix: 'about a WAPE point' is a one-significant-figure statement and 0.602 rounds to 1 under the convention this audit has already ratified; both operands (0.521, 0.515) are printed in the same sentence. The rewrite is permissible as a precision improvement but must not be logged as an error correction. 4) Line 382, first pass proposed replacing '~2 WAPE points' on the grounds that it is 4x too loose. REJECTED as an error correction: the sentence is an upper bound and the measured maximum is 0.472 points, so the claim is TRUE. Marking it THESIS_WRONG would record a defect where none exists. 5) Line 175, first pass proposed replacing 'typically under 2 WAPE points' with a 1-minute-only bound. REJECTED as an error correction: 16 of the 20 grid cells satisfy the hedged bound and the chapter separately acknowledges the larger sub-minute gaps at line 386. 6) Generally: do NOT recompute any of the relative-edge percentages at line 411 from the rounded cells of tab:pred-wape -- e.g. (146.1-98.8)/146.1 from the printed table gives 32.4% only by coincidence at that cell, while (54.16-52.92)/54.16 from printed 54.2/52.9 gives 2.40% against the true 2.30%.
